subject: Post-demo decision playbook, priority tests, and control-path probes
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood-inference.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan@cloudhealth.ai>, Harpreet Singh <harpreet@cloudhealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo decision playbook, priority tests, and control-path probes

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap and suggested decision playbook so we’re all aligned on next steps.

Key pains you reiterated
- Inference cost and predictable unit economics for high-volume batch reports
- Need sub-100ms p95 for short synchronous queries in the triage UI
- Auditability for PHI-related logs and strict retention controls

Primary goals we heard
1) Proof the model can meet the 95th%-tile latency target on your 2k qps bursts
2) Validate cost at scale (tokens per dollar) with 30-day run projections
3) Demonstrate audit log exports and retention pipeline into your S3/KMS setup

Proposed decision playbook (recommended order)
A. Smoke tests (this week): short TTL latency runs + sanity correctness checks (Karthik to own test spec)
B. Control-path probes (next week): KV cache priming, routing to cheaper model variants under burst, and fallback behavior
C. Full-ish bakeoff (2–3 days): parallel runs vs competitor baseline for throughput/cost

Immediate asks for CloudHealth AI
- Can you confirm the test window windows you have for a 2–3 hr smoke on Mon/Tue next week?
- Please share a minimal sample of your request distribution (histogram or example traces).

Attachments: redwood-demo-summary.pdf (PDF) — quick TL;DR from the demo; control-path-test-specs.xlsx — tentative test matrix.

Next steps I’ll take:
- Karthik will circulate a tight tech checklist and runbook by EOD Monday.
- I’ll provision a dedicated test slot and share access + a pre-signed s3 location for logs.

Thanks — feel free to flag any missing pieces.

—
Camila Reyes
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood-inference.com
Redwood Inference
From: Megan Liu <megan@cloudhealth.ai>

Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo decision playbook, priority tests, and control-path probes

Camila — thanks for the succinct recap. That playbook looks reasonable. A couple clarifying items before we lock test windows: 

1) For the 2k qps bursts, can you confirm whether the latency SLAs are measured cold-start inclusive or with warmed KV cache? We need clarity for our SRE acceptance criteria.
2) Response logs: we have to confirm fields that will be exported (request id, model variant, raw tokens redacted flag). Any chance Karthik can include the exact schema in the runbook?

We’re available for a 3-hour window on Monday 2026-08-17, 10:00–13:00 PT. That works for the engineering team.

Also attaching the brief procurement checklist (see inline) — we’ll attempt to push NDA and procurement internally this week.

—
Megan Liu
Director of Platform Engineering, CloudHealth AI
megan@cloudhealth.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan@cloudhealth.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo decision playbook, priority tests, and control-path probes

Megan — quick technical clarifications inline and the minimal spec attached.

1) Latency measurement: our p95 figure in the demo was with a warmed-hot KV cache (typical for low-latency path). For the smoke run we’ll do two passes: 
  - Pass A: warmed cache (15–30m warm-up period, synthetic priming)
  - Pass B: mixed cold/warm start profile representative of your trace samples

2) Logs schema (summary):
  - request_id (UUID)
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - model_variant (string)
  - tokens_in / tokens_out (ints)
  - latency_ms (int)
  - trace_sample (optional, redacted)
  - phI_tag (boolean) — Redwood will NOT store raw PHI; we will surface redacted flags only.

Attached: control-path-test-specs.xlsx — row-level test cases, metrics to capture, and quick command snippets.

I’ll be on the Mon 10:00–13:00 PT window and will run the smoke harness with your SRE. Marissa — I’ll need a signed NDA before we push live logs to your S3.

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Inference Performance
karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com

- Audit log delivery: default is daily S3 pushes; if you need streaming we can discuss an adapter but that will require additional ops time.

Megan — confirm NDA routing and we’ll get the S3 pre-signed creds ready ahead of the Monday run.

Great — thanks everyone for the quick alignment. Final checklist before Monday’s window (10:00–13:00 PT):
- Megan: confirm sample trace upload to the Drive link by EOD Sunday (we used the HubSpot link above).
- Harpreet: share any SRE firewall egress allowlist entries we should add for the test IPs.
- Marissa: we’ll sign the NDA and return scans as soon as CloudHealth legal confirms redlines.

I’ll send a short runbook email 90 minutes before the test with the exact cluster endpoints and the pre-signed S3 log location. Expected outputs from the smoke run: p95 latency tables, per-variant cost breakdown, and a raw log drop.

If anything changes please flag on this thread. Looking forward to productive tests — we’ll bring two stack engineers and a runbook operator.

—
Camila Reyes
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
